sources.entry: FreshRSS - Self-hostable RSS feed aggregator. (Demo, Source Code) AGPL-3.0 PHP/Docker

summary.one_liner: FreshRSS is a self-hosted, multi-user RSS/Atom feed aggregator written in PHP that can also scrape websites with XPath and expose APIs for mobile and native feed reader apps.
summary.what_it_does: FreshRSS aggregates RSS and Atom feeds in a web interface that supports multiple users, an anonymous reading mode, and custom tags. It receives instant push updates from WebSub-compatible sources and can scrape sites without feeds using XPath, and it also parses JSON documents. Users can reshare article selections as HTML, RSS, or OPML. Login options include a web form (with an anonymous option), HTTP authentication (compatible with proxy delegation), and OpenID Connect. It provides a Google Reader API and a Fever API for third-party clients, plus a command-line interface, and it supports extensions. The README lists a table of compatible apps and a translation status for 20+ languages.
use_cases: aggregate blogs and news sites in one place
read feeds in a mobile app via sync API
share curated article lists with others
multi-user feed reading on a home server
how_to_run: Get FreshRSS with git or by downloading the archive
Put the application on your server, exposing only the ./p/ folder to the web
Give the web server user write access to the ./data/ folder
Open FreshRSS in a browser and follow the installation process (or use the Command-Line Interface)
For Apache, enable AllowEncodedSlashes for better mobile client compatibility
Advanced settings: copy from config.default.php into data/config.php
stack: PHP extensions: cURL, DOM, JSON, XML, session, ctype
notable: Google Reader API and Fever API let many native apps on Linux, Android, iOS, Windows, and macOS sync with it
WebSub support for instant push updates from compatible sources
Built-in XPath-based web scraping for sites without feeds
Runs on low-power hardware; README says it works on a Raspberry Pi 1
Available as a rolling edge branch or a more stable latest branch
caveats: Manual install requires a web server, PHP 8.2+, and a database setup; an automated install option is referenced but not detailed in the README
Fever API has limited features and is described as less efficient and less safe than the Google Reader API
The edge branch gets newest features but is less stable; the latest branch receives fewer fixes and no backports
